summary:
The core rule held under attack: I found no way for a revoked device's approval or reconciliation answer to start a new action, compensation or out-of-cone observation. A 160-seed random interleaving fuzz on real bodies, checked against an oracle re-derived from the ledger alone, found no violation, no stranded mission and no ledger break (the same oracle fires on pr196 in 1 of 6 seeds).

Four things need fixing before this is relied on, all reproduced on real bodies at head f35b7986:

1. **A completed compensation is mis-recorded after a revocation.** If the body dies between the Gate's receipt and the mission's record, and the approving device is revoked before the restart, the founder is asked to approve a compensation that already ran. A reject records it as DECLINED. pr196 records DONE from the receipt, so this is a regression.
2. **The integrity review blames the device for founder-approved dispatches.** Once the device's approval was withdrawn and the founder approved the re-ask, that later dispatch is listed as resting on the device. It happens in the late-suspicion path and after a standing-approval regression.
3. **A device-signed ABANDON keeps dispatching compensations after the revocation.** The decision record mentions it under open question 3, but no test pins it and neither `greg status` nor the review shows it.
4. **The mutation gate has gaps.** 16 of my 18 mutants not on the builder's list pass all 50 tests. Three of them remove authority safeguards: one lets the void of a device's reconciliation answer take the founder's approval of the action, and two make the appraiser refute honest closures.

Two smaller points: a revocation waiting in the inbox does not stop dispatches that have not started in the same turn (disclosed in the decision record), and a key marked as a suspected compromise can be delegated again with no friction.

Boundaries are clean: no protected artifact is in the diff, `greg/founder.py` and `greg/authority.py` are unchanged, and the integrity check, the five required test files (107 passed), `acceptance check` and the directive ratchet all pass.

Not run: the whole suite, the builder's 68-mutant gate, hosted CI, the phone page, and composition with #290, #291, #273 or #278. The fuzz does not cover goals or restores. The uncertain-dispatch variant of finding 1 is from reading the code only.

Probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/rdr-probes and logs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/rdr-logs. My detached worktree is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/rd-review; the builder's worktree and the main checkout were not touched.

findings.title: A compensation completed before the revocation is not settled from its receipt; a founder reject then records it as DECLINED
findings.claim: A device approves a compensation (superseded mission). The Gate dispatches it and writes a positive receipt; the body dies before `mission.compensated` is recorded; the founder revokes the device while the body is down. On restart the branch records nothing for the completed compensation and opens a new APPROVAL ask for it, whose text says 'the executed effect stands; nothing is run for it'. If the founder rejects, the ledger records `mission.compensated` DECLINED with no receipt, although the effect happened and its Gate receipt exists. On pr196 the same sequence records DONE from the retained receipt, so this is a regression against 'Revocation must not ... pretend an external effect never happened'. The Gate never dispatches twice. Cause: actions are settled from the Gate's record by `_recover_dispatch` whatever the approval state; a compensation has no such recovery and goes back through `_run_compensation`, which asks again (SUPERSEDED branch) or reaches `AuthorityOffice.act`, which answers OUTSIDE_SCOPE before it looks for the retained receipt. The decision record's section 'A dispatch already in flight' says the restarted body settles such a dispatch from the Gate's record; that is true for actions only. By reading, not run: a claim without a receipt (died mid-dispatch) takes the same path and can also end as DECLINED.

findings.suggested_fix: In `MissionEngine._run_compensation` (greg/missions.py), before the open-ask, rejected-scope, SUPERSEDED and `office.act` branches, read the compensation's own proposal from the Gate: `self.office.prior(self.office.proposal_id(scope, f"compensate:{aid}:{original}"))`. A receipt is recorded as `mission.compensated` from that receipt; a claim without a receipt is recorded UNCERTAIN and raises the COMPENSATION ask, as the un-revoked path does. This needs no change to greg/authority.py. Add the probe as a test (it fails today) and a mutant for the lookup, and correct the decision record's in-flight section.

findings.title: The integrity review lists founder-approved dispatches as resting on the revoked device
findings.claim: `build_review` in greg/revocation.py bounds its action loop at the point where the device's approval stopped standing (`end`), but its Gate-grant loop has no such bound: every grant of that scope issued after the device's DECISION and before the reviewed revocation record, and not accounted for by the bounded action loop, is listed as 'a dispatch the Gate granted under its approval, not yet recorded by the mission when the key was revoked'. So when the device's approval was withdrawn and the founder approved the re-ask, the founder's dispatch is attributed to the device. Both halves of the row are false: the founder approved it and the mission recorded it. It happens in two paths: (a) a suspicion signed after a plain revocation (`marks_revocation`), and (b) an immediate suspected-compromise revocation after the standing-approval regression (`autonomy.regress`) withdrew the device's approval. The work brief required the review to list the device's commands and resting effects and nothing else.

findings.suggested_fix: Bound the grant loop the way the action loop is bounded: count only grants issued before the ledger position where the device's approval stopped standing (the request's first `decision.withdrawn`, or the revocation that voided it; for a late suspicion that is the marked revocation, not the marking record), and exclude grants that any recorded action or observation accounts for at any position. Add both probes as tests. My mutants R5 (`end = cut`) and R31 (grants read past the revocation) pass all 50 tests today and should then be caught.

findings.title: A mission a revoked device abandoned keeps dispatching compensations after the revocation, and no surface shows it
findings.claim: A device delegated LIFECYCLE signs ABANDONED for a mission whose executed write has a signed compensation; the founder's DEVICE_REVOKE reaches the body in the same inbox read. On the following turns the body dispatches the compensation through the Gate (a new grant after `device.revoked`), solely because of the revoked key's command. This is the same shape as the builder's own reproduction (command and revocation before the next turn; the effect runs). The decision record names it in open question 3 ('compensations run after an abandon'; default: nothing is paused or undone), so the default is disclosed. But unlike a resume: no test pins it; `greg status` shows nothing for it (`resumed_and_still_running` covers resumes only, and the row has `voided_requests: []`); and the suspected-compromise review, read as the revocation left the ledger, lists only 'a mission lifecycle it set' and never the compensation that ran afterwards.

findings.suggested_fix: This is the founder's decision, like the resume question; put it to him as its own question rather than a parenthesis. Without changing the default: pin it with a test, and list per revocation in `revocation.summary` the missions the key ended whose `mission.compensation_required` facts are not yet closed, as `resumed_and_still_running` does for resumes. Alternative default: hold compensations not yet dispatched for a mission a revoked device ended behind one founder ask.

findings.title: Three authority safeguards have no failing test: their mutants pass all 50 tests
findings.claim: The project standard is that every safeguard has a test that fails without it. Three mutants of the new code that the builder's gate does not list pass the whole test file (50 passed each). R1: in `MissionBook._revoked`, `if m is not None and approval:` becomes `if m is not None:`; the void of a device's unrecorded reconciliation answer then also removes the action's approved scope, including a founder's approval (a RECONCILIATION ask carries the action's scope digest). R3: in `appraisal._signer_revoked` the key comparison is removed; the appraiser then refutes an honest closure when any other device was revoked between approval and dispatch. R4: in the same function the lower bound `answer_seq <` is removed; a fresh approval from a re-delegated key is then refuted for the key's earlier revocation. The real code is right in all three cases: my probes B1, C3 and C4 pass on it and each fails under its mutant.

findings.title: Thirteen more mutants of the review, the status and the trail survive; no test mentions a compensation

Two of my eighteen were caught (R12, R20). findings.title: A revocation waiting in the inbox does not stop dispatches that have not started in the same turn
findings.claim: Two missions each hold the phone's approval of a write. The founder's DEVICE_REVOKE file reaches the inbox after the first mission's dispatch, while the turn is still running. The second mission's write, not yet started, still runs in that turn on the phone's approval; the revocation is applied only at the next turn's inbox read. The body already reads the inbox before every mission step for BODY_STOP (`Body._stop_now`), but not for DEVICE_REVOKE. The decision record discloses this ('Mission steps later in the same turn still use the approvals as that turn began'); the builder's report describes only a dispatch in flight. With paid workers that run for minutes, one turn can be long, and the founder's word was 'immediately'.

findings.suggested_fix: Founder question 9 should say this plainly. If he wants it closed: authenticate pending DEVICE_REVOKE commands in the same between-steps inbox read that already takes BODY_STOP, and rebuild the book before the next mission step. That touches the turn loop, which #273 also changes.

findings.title: A key marked as a suspected compromise can be delegated again while its review is open
findings.claim: After `DEVICE_REVOKE` with `suspected_compromise: true`, a founder-signed DEVICE_ENROLL of the same key is accepted with no warning while the integrity review is still unanswered, and the key's new approvals run. It is the founder's own signed command, so no authority is bypassed. But the body now knows the key is suspected, and `greg.body.device_delegations` itself says a compromised device gets a new key, because a token the key holder forward-dated cannot be told from a new one after re-delegation.

findings.suggested_fix: Put it to the founder: refuse DEVICE_ENROLL for a key whose latest revocation is marked suspected (or whose review is unanswered), or accept it and say so on the enrolment result and in the status.

checked_and_clean: Authority after revocation, random search: 160 seeds x 50 operations on real bodies (three standing gated missions, two devices; approve or reject by founder, phone or laptop, by direct apply or inbox file; plain and suspected revocation; re-enrolment; body restart; body and mission pause and resume by founder or device; drift). An oracle re-derived from the ledger alone found no Gate grant marked founder-approved that rested only on a revoked device's approval. 160 passed in 584 s. The same oracle fires on pr196 in 1 of 6 seeds. Probe: rdr-probes/test_probe_fuzz.py.

Same fuzz, other invariants at every step or at the end: the ledger chain verifies; no mission is stranded (the founder resumes and approves what is open, and every note is written unless he rejected); one trail record per (request, revocation); the engine's book, a fresh MissionBook and the founder_facts book agree on approved scopes, voided and consumed.
The builder's 50 tests pass on the head (23 s). The final test file copied onto pr196 gives 42 failed, 8 passed, and the reproduction fails on `assert not note.exists()`, as reported.

Every DECISION kind, by reading: only `_apply_answer` adds to approved_scopes; all four `AuthorityOffice.act` call sites (action, compensation, out-of-cone observation, declined-if sensor) pass the fold's set; the office keeps no approval state of its own. APPROVAL, SENSOR_SCOPE and RECONCILIATION are voided; the other kinds confer no Gate scope.
A compensation approved by a device that is revoked before the dispatch does not run, is asked again under a new request, and runs once on the founder's approval (probe F1).
The void of a device's unrecorded reconciliation answer leaves the founder's approval of the action in place, and the retry runs on it (probe B1).

Ordering and replay: a decision delivered after the revocation is rejected; a replayed envelope is rejected; approve-then-revoke in one inbox read voids; a re-enrolled key revives nothing and its fresh approval works. Covered by the fuzz and by the builder's tests, which I read and ran.
History: the (seq, hash) of every ledger event before the revocation is identical after the revocation, the trail and the review; verify_chain passes (probe B2).

Exactly-once for actions: `_recover_dispatch` settles an interrupted action from the Gate's own record whatever the approval state (read; the builder's test for it passes). The compensation case is the exception reported above.

Malformed DEVICE_REVOKE through the inbox of a paused body: 12 bodies (non-text key id, missing key id, suspected_compromise as None, 1, 'true' or [true], an extra field, a 15,000-character key id, an unknown key with the flag) are all REJECTED; the body keeps turning and the device stays delegated (probe B4).
A second suspicion for the same revocation, a suspicion for a key never delegated, and a suspicion naming the founder's own key are refused; one review and two revocation records result (probe B5).

A review of a device that signed DECISION approve and reject, LIFECYCLE, BODY_PAUSE and BODY_RESUME builds as OPEN_FOR_FOUNDER_REVIEW, lists exactly those commands in order with signature_verifies true, and the founder is offered its answer (probe B2). I found no device-signable accepted command that makes `build_review` raise.
Appraiser, real code: another device's revocation between approval and dispatch, and a re-delegated key's fresh approval, both give VERIFIED with no findings (probes C3, C4).

Flooding and crash loops: `settle` writes each trail and review once (keyed facts, checked before writing); the wording screen withholds rather than raises; `Journal.record` has no size limit that a long review could hit.

Boundaries: none of the 13 protected artifacts is in the diff; greg/founder.py (DEVICE_KINDS) and greg/authority.py are unchanged; no new command kind. `python -m governance.integrity --check` reports 13 protected artifacts, all as authorized, exit 0.

Required checks on head f35b7986: test_repo_health_gates, test_effect_call_allowlist, test_governance_integrity, test_greg_packaging and test_sources_parse give 107 passed; `python -m acceptance check` is sound, exit 0; `python -m acceptance directive --against 8d205324...` exits 0.

Neighbouring files on the head: test_greg_device_class, test_greg_mission_book_incremental, test_greg_standing_approval_regression, test_greg_remote and integration test_greg_device_revocation_process give 56 passed.

My mutant runner is sound: the builder's own mutant 'the fold ignores a device revocation' is CAUGHT through it (27 failed), and every survivor I report shows '50 passed', not an import or collection error.
The decision record lists eleven open questions, as the ledger entry and intent record say. The builder's worktree is clean at f35b7986 and was not touched.
